subject.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers

question: Should native OpenClaw plugin manifests permanently declare executable `mcpServers`, with user configuration overriding same-named servers and plugin disablement detaching them?
rationale: The field expands the public plugin manifest and runtime activation contract; tests can prove mechanics but cannot decide whether this is the intended long-term ownership and precedence model.

options.title: Approve manifest-owned servers
options.body: Keep `mcpServers`, document activation and precedence as public API, and add contract-focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Use existing configuration only
options.body: Remove the manifest field and require plugins to guide users toward `mcp.servers` configuration or an existing runtime registration seam.

options.title: Narrow to an experimental seam
options.body: Keep the capability behind an explicitly experimental plugin API until activation and upgrade semantics are settled.

recommendation.title: Approve manifest-owned servers
recommendation.body: Keep `mcpServers`, document activation and precedence as public API, and add contract-focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history introduced node-hosted plugin MCP server support and owns the adjacent manifest/runtime surfaces.
